messages:
rob_sales: FYI HelixHealth wants a 3-week POC. Model: clinicx-13b-lite (custom variant). Requirements: SentencePiece 64k, support for mixed-int4/int8 fallback, CMEK (HSM), and embedding endpoint for search. They want p50 ~120ms single-user.
talia_se: Noted. clinicx-13b-lite isn't in our catalog yet. We'll need a variant compatibility check + tokenizer parity. Ask them for the .spm and sample corpus.
marc_infra: Primary runtime risk: mixed quant path and embedding endpoint isolation. Embeddings use a separate quant profile in our runtime; need to validate memory working set for simultaneous gen+embed. I can run a small dedicated rig to test both together.
rob_sales: They also asked about routing: can we route generation to Dedicated quant nodes and embeddings to a smaller cheap pool?
marc_infra: Yes, routing policy can map routes to different pools. For POC we can pin generation to a quantized Dedicated pool and route embeddings to a CPU-optimized or smaller GPU pool. Will validate tail-latency.
emma_sec: Security checklist: HelixHealth requests HSM-backed CMEK, dataset ingestion controls, and an exportable audit trail. Draft answer: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS, configurable audit log export, and ingestion controls. Keys are customer-controlled and rotations are supported; Redwood does not retain plaintext keys. SOC2 artifacts can be shared under NDA."
rob_sales: Can you also confirm if key rotation causes endpoint reloads? They worry about UX during rotation.
emma_sec: Rotation can be scheduled; swapping keys may require an endpoint reload < 45s unless they use warm-reload plan. We'll include a runbook.
talia_se: Test plan: tokenizer parity, mixed-quant stability (int4 primary, int8 fallback), embedding+gen co-run perf for seq=64/256 and embed batch sizes [1,8]. Metrics: p50/p95 latency gen+embed, memory OOM flags, tokenization mismatch rate, embedding cosine drift vs fp16 baseline.
marc_infra: Kicking off sweep. Config snippet: ```model: clinicx-13b-lite
quant_profile: mixed_int4_int8
endpoints: [generation, embeddings]
seqs: [64,256]
embed_batches: [1,8]
metrics: [p50_gen,p95_gen,p50_embed,oom,perp_delta,embed_cosine_delta]```
rob_sales: Great. Also they asked for a POC quote (infra + 12 eng hours + compliance review). Give rough delta int4 vs fp16?
marc_infra: Rough: mixed-int quant profile often yields 25-40% cost reduction vs fp16 for throughput-heavy gen. Embedding costs are separate; will provide numbers after the sweep.
rob_sales: @ops_bot please open ticket and set ETA 72h.
ops_bot: Ticket created: RINF-14567 - "HelixHealth / clinicx-13b-lite POC compatibility + mixed-quant sweep". Assignee: marc_infra. ETA: 72h.
talia_se: I'll request their SentencePiece export and a 300-prompt sample focused on clinical Q&A and embedding queries. If tokenizer mismatch occurs, fallback options: canonical tokenizer import, or run an fp16 canary for the POC.
rob_sales: Thanks team. I'll draft the POC quote including the SOC blurb and routing options. Ping here when results are in. :thumbsup:
